headline: Recommended holding a request for a joint committee meeting on the city's pavement management plan, 3-0.
summary: Councilors and city staff discussed the city's 2025 Pavement Management Plan, including road condition ratings, repair methods, and funding. Councilors and residents also raised concerns about sidewalks, drainage, and contractor inspections. The committee then voted 3-0 to recommend holding the request for the joint meeting.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 19, 2026 Traffic and Parking Committee meeting, 3-0.
Recommended holding the request for a joint meeting with the Standing Committee on Public Works to review the city's pavement management plan, 3-0.

. Miscellaneous Item 3 
August 25, 2026 Page 2 of 6Traffic and Parking Committee
Order of Councilor Tony Economou - Request Standing Committee on Public Works 
meet jointly with the Standing Committee on Traffic and Parking for the purpose of 
reviewing and discussing the city’s strategic pavement management plan. Further, 
request Commissioner of Public Works and Commissioner of Transportation and 
Mobility attend the joint committee meeting to present the city’s 2025 Pavement 
Management, prepared by Apex Companies, LLC and Cyvl.ai. (see attached).
# 12m CC July 21, 2026
a.
August 25, 2026 Page 3 of 6Traffic and Parking Committee
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Public 
Works, who provided an overview of the item, including how the Department of Transportation 
and Mobility and Department of Public Works collaborate for the city’s pavement management 
plan.
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and 
the Assistant Commissioner of Public Works, who provided a presentation relative to the city’s 
street construction and pavement management program. Said presentation included information 
concerning the importance of pavement preservation, advanced and flexible project planning and 
project selections based on pavement condition index (PCI) data, the process relative to developing 
the 2025 Pavement Management Plan, an overview of how to classify road PCI with estimated 
treatment costs, impacts of pavement preservation on PCI, the importance of performing 
routine/preventative maintenance to avoid road deterioration, the requirement for major 
rehabilitation with the goal to maintain the majority lowest road classification at eighty (80) PCI, 
monetary advantages associated with maintaining acceptable road conditions over a longer period 
of time, the 2023 average PCI of the city’s road network rated at 69.6 with the estimated cost at 
$19.4 million annually towards pavement management to fix the worst classified roads first , 
considerations to inflation since 2023 with an estimated thirty percent (30%) increase for 
pavement management supplies and labor, the 2023 estimated cost at $16.2 million annually 
towards pavement management by following a balanced pavement preservation program, and 
routine maintenance options to maintain roads at eighty (80) to ninety (90) PCI such as crack seal , 
fog seal, and permanent patch methods.
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the whether the 
permanent long patch program addresses issues related to manholes with the Assistant 
Commissioner of Public Works.
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed concerns related to the 
chip seal treatment method, feasible alternative treatment options in lieu of chip seal, best 
practices for using chip seal, benefits to using the cape seal treatment method, cost differentials 
between chip and cape seal methods, and subsequent treatment limitations after using the cape 
seal and microsurfacing methods with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering and 
Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility. 
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized Councilor Bilotta, who discussed concerns related to 
excess chips impacting stormwater infrastructure, issues related to hot in place recycling 
treatment, cold in place recycling and mill and overlay treatment methods with the Assistant 
Commissioner of Public Works.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the feasibility of cape sealing and microsurfacing 
roadways that did not withstand chip seal with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed pavement management 
budget allocations available for piloting cape seal treatment methods with the Assistant 
Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke concerning when the 
projects associated with street and sidewalk selections made by district councilors would begin, as 
well as project delays due to utility holds with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering , 
Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility, and Commissioner of Public Works. 
August 25, 2026 Page 4 of 6Traffic and Parking Committee
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed the street and sidewalk 
resurfacing process, whether there have been changes to the inspection process for street 
construction projects and challenges related to construction work done by utility companies with 
the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and the Assistant Commissioner of Public 
Works.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed issues with the process used to inspect contracted 
work, the ability to hold said contractors accountable for the quality of the work performed , 
communication methods used to inform residents of scheduled roadwork, and the process used by 
residents to obtain specific project information with accompanying contact information to file a 
complaint/express concerns with Councilor Ojeda and Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized Councilor Bilotta, who highlighted the importance of 
holding contractors to higher standards and a timeline of roads in each district identified to be 
treated with crack seal with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering and Commissioner of 
Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou then recognized the following Speakers:
1. Maria Kaplanes, Worcester resident, spoke neither in favor of nor opposed to the item
2. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke neither in favor of nor opposed to the item
Chairperson Councilor Rivera discussed the poor sidewalk conditions, construction status, and 
drainage issues on Coombs Rd. with Speaker #1, Traffic and Parking Committee Member 
Councilor Ojeda, and Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the benefits and positive progress made since 
establishing the city’s pavement management program and highlighted challenges associated with 
inflation with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Mitra, who highlighted the importance of 
improving processes in the city to create a more inviting community for residents and business 
owners, the feasibility of resurfacing major arteries in the city in the next three (3) to four (4) 
years, the process used for District Councilors to select streets /sidewalks for resurfacing, and the 
process used to allocate funds for each street /sidewalk selected for resurfacing with the 
Commissioner of Public Works and Principal for Apex Companies. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the benefits of establishing a pavement preservation 
program, highlighted the notion that significant pavement preservation results takes time, and the 
impact of an insufficient pavement preservation program with the Commissioner of 
Transportation and Mobility.
Chairperson Councilor Rivera discussed how many streets in the city fell into each PCI 
classification, the process used to fund the city’s various pavement projects, and the number of 
streets in the city’s road network with the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and 
Principal for Apex Companies.
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke concerning Fiscal 
Year 2027 (FY27) resurfacing budget allocations, Massachusetts Department of Transportation 
(MassDOT) funding opportunities associated with resurfacing Grafton St ., and why twenty -one
